name: Joseph Jacks
title: RT by @JosephJacks_: Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B has been dethroned A model that runs 30 of its 40 layers as convolutions instead of attention just took the top spot on the Agon bench. @liquidai LFM2.5-24B-A2B is their own architecture, and it is not another Qwen finetune. 24B total with 2B active per token, 64 experts routed top-4, and its own 128K tokenizer, expanded in place from LFM2's 65K. The Qwen models on this board use 151,936 tokens on an all-attention stack. Nothing here shares that ancestry. It scores 185 of 198 on the composite, which is 93.4%, first of 23 models with a complete set of runs. Agent 91.7%, code 93.3%, reasoning 96.1%. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, which has held first place at 89.9%, is now second. 14.5 GB at Q4_K_M, which fits an 8GB card with the expert layers offloaded to CPU. One configuration note, on the record rather than buried. I run it off the card's default originally, and some failures from overthinking were rerun with reasoning constraints matching all other models run on the benchmark. Note that Liquid post-trained this model with agentic RL inside @NousResearch Hermes Agent, by name, and Hermes is the harness Agon runs on. A model tuned against the same tool surface the benchmark exercises starts with an advantage, so read the agent number with that in mind. Median 5,506 generated tokens per request, 67 of 68 requests over 1,000, decoded at 25.4 tok/s. Wins in speed and score. If a 2B-active convolution model can lead this board, what is the attention stack buying?

name: RedTeam / Innerworks
title: "We're not afraid of hyper-intelligent bot swarms on the internet. We use them to optimise our technology." When we launched RedTeam almost two years ago we could clearly see where the internet was heading. We've since seen clients with over 90% of their traffic made up of not just automation but highly intelligent bot swarms, capable of bypassing any traditional detection mechanism. The only way to combat a threat like this is to welcome it and learn from it. By constantly ingesting and evolving attack vectors from a hive mind of miners, a Bittensor powered defence has now become the only reliable source of protection on the internet.

title: The future of cybersecurity will be dictated by a defender's ability to not only ingest unique attacks, but generate the strains that don't exist yet and ship the detection ahead of them. As the rest of the industry degrades, the largest financial institutions will consolidate on the single provider that can do this at scale. That provider needs a constant supply of unique attacks to work from, and a subnet is the only structure that pays a swarm of attackers to supply them. bittensor:native #SN61
